chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said, on the authority of Ali ibn al-'Abbas, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, on the authority of Abu Ibrahim Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) that he said:

Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, was ever without time and without place, and He is now as He was. No place is free from Him, nor is any place occupied by Him, nor does He dwell in any place. Wherever there is a secret counsel of three, He is the fourth; and of five, He is the sixth; and of fewer or more, He is with them wherever they are. There is no veil between Him and His creation other than His creation. He veiled Himself without a veil, being veiled; and He concealed Himself without a covering, being concealed. There is no god but He, the Great, the Exalted.
ai.seo_question: What does Shia theology say about Allah's relationship with time and space?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (as) articulates the doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence) by affirming Allah's eternity beyond *zaman* (time) and *makan** (space), distinguishing His essential presence from physical containment. This narration serves as a foundational text in Shia theology for refuting anthropomorphism (*Tajsim*) and spatial localization, emphasizing that while He is with all things, He is not mixed with them. The description of being 'hidden by non-hiding' underscores the paradox of divine nearness and remoteness, a key theme in *Usul al-Kafi* and *al-Tawhid*.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 12. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma`il al-Barmaki said, on the authority of `Ali ibn al`Abbas, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Ya`qub ibn Ja`fari that Abu Ibrahim Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Kadhim) (as) said: "

Verily, Allah (swt) was always without time and space, and He was like He was. No place is free from Him, nor is any place occupied by Him, nor des He dissolve in any place. Nowhere is there a secret counsel between three persons but He is the fourth of them, nor (between) five but He is the sixth of them, nor less than that nor more but He is with them where so ever they are. There is no veil between Him and His Creation other than His Creation. He is Veiled without a Veil, and He is Covered without a Cover. There is no god but He, the Great, the Exalted."
